CHIEF COMPLAINT
Back pain and tingling in right foot

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports onset of back pain and pins and needles sensation in right foot yesterday while raking leaves. Back tightening began approximately two hours after coming inside the house. Patient has experienced similar back pain approximately three years ago which resolved after one day. Current pain is somewhat relieved by heat (hot shower) and worsens with forward bending. Pain slightly improves when sitting. Patient has already tried ice and two advils without relief. Tingling is localized to the right leg. Patient reports pain when bending over but denies pain when standing up.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Back pain approximately three years ago that resolved after one day.

MEDICATIONS
Advil - two tablets tried for current pain without relief.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports no regular physical activity and considers raking leaves unusual activity for himself.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Pain noted with forward flexion. No pain with extension. Pain with palpation at L5. Dorsiflexion normal. Pulses equal in all extremities.

RESULTS
X-ray of low back: normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Probable low back strain. Patient advised to rest. Meloxicam prescribed. Physical therapy referral for stretching and exercises to improve conditioning given sedentary lifestyle. Follow-up in two weeks with callback if no improvement. If no improvement at two weeks, consider MRI.
